situation:
You are a first-time renter with no credit history who has just moved to a city where rent runs far higher than at home. Your new job pays $2,600 a month after taxes, and the apartment you and a roommate signed for costs $1,450. The judge is a financial coach at PINE STREET CREDIT UNION.

Because you have no credit history, the landlord required an extra month's rent as a deposit. You are $900 short of the move-in total. You have tracked your spending in a spreadsheet for a year, and the credit union offers a budgeting app that would move money to savings automatically on payday.

SPLITPAY, a pay-in-four service advertised constantly on the feeds you scroll, would cover the furniture and the extra deposit in installments and close the $900 shortfall. It reports a missed installment to the credit reporting companies, which would damage the credit record you have not started building, and its fees cost more than paying outright.

The coach (judge) has asked you to recommend how to close the $900 shortfall and how to save automatically before spending. Using SPLITPAY to cover the furniture and the extra deposit in installments damages the credit record you have not started building. Buying secondhand furniture and setting an automatic transfer to savings before spending means your roommate covers the extra deposit and waits months to be repaid.

The coach (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are a financial coach at PINE STREET CREDIT UNION. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You have asked the new renter to recommend how the $900 shortfall gets closed, whether the spreadsheet or the budgeting app is the better tool for a first budget in a costlier city, and how a saving transfer happens before the spending rather than after it.

During the presentation you are to ask the participant the following questions:
judgeQuestions: Who ends up carrying the cost of this choice?
Is that fair to your roommate, and how would you make it right?
